propositions: The T11 POST-ROLLBACK SCHEMA STATE paragraph generates high-volume tautological findings (~8 of 21) that obscure real bugs, particularly for append-only stores

An unconditional post-rollback-state advisory is replaced with a four-condition applicability rule: interpretation change, in-place rewrite, read-path removal, or one-way transformation with no back-out
Purely additive backward-compatible persistence changes (new record types, optional fields, new tables/columns with defaults) are explicitly excluded from post-rollback findings as false positives
The applicability rule names no specific store technology, making it portable across SQL migrations, event stores, document databases, and config formats
New contract tests verify the four conditions are present, the old unconditional wording is gone, and the anti-FP line for additive changes is included
